# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: empty-seed first candidate for the tau2 airline capability. Diagnosed all 10 val tasks via 3 parallel read-only subagents (one per failure cluster), then shipped a MIX of edit types in one candidate: 2 new read tools (find_reservations, get_price_quote), in-body guards/enriched errors/enriched returns on existing tools, and a policy contract. Not yet scored.
- Key structural finding: reward basis is DB+COMMUNICATE (averaged). DB failures dominate (7 of the failing tasks), but task 11 is DB-correct and fails only COMMUNICATE — so surfacing engine-computed amounts in tool returns is a distinct, cheap lever. Action-trace [MISS] lines are often spurious (extra dict keys on flights) and must not be optimized against — only db_check/communicate_checks matter.
- Highest-leverage lever this run looks like the wrong-reservation CAPABILITY-GAP (tasks 17/22 are consistent hard-0): a model with no route-based reservation lookup guesses the first id. A read tool + prose may not be enough if the model doesn't call it — the fallback lever is an in-body write guard that rejects a write whose route doesn't match the reservation.
- What to try next iteration: read the gate RESULT; for any cluster that didn't move, escalate from "read tool + prose" to "code guard on the write path" (cluster A) or "composite confirm->write tool" (cluster E).

## Iteration cand_0002
- Strategy tried: build on cand_0001 (rejected, +0.100, broke nothing). The gate's own note said the lever is POWER/SIZE, not redesign — so I KEPT the four edits that did no damage (cancel guard, enriched book error, enriched update returns, policy contract) and REPLACED only the weakest: cand_0001's cluster-A fix was a NEW read tool (`find_reservations`) that a mid-tier model can simply never call. I moved that fix onto the ALWAYS-called `get_user_details` as a return enrichment (`reservations_detail`), so the disambiguating route info is unskippable. Not yet scored.
- Key process lesson: for a mid-capability reader, prefer enriching a tool it is already forced to call over adding an optional tool it must choose to call. An "add a read tool + tell it to call it" fix is only as strong as the model's compliance; moving the same information into an unavoidable return is strictly more powerful for the same blast radius.
- Plateau/stall signal: none yet (1 prior RESULT). If cand_0002 is also rejected with no damage AND 17/22 are still hard-0, that means the model sees `reservations_detail` and still picks wrong — then the only remaining lever is forcing the write path to validate the target (hard, since write tools only get reservation_id), or a composite resolve-then-write tool.
- What to try next iteration: read the RESULT. If cluster E (narrate-without-action) or task 23's cert-split still fail, switch from prose to a composite split-booking WRITE tool (issue N one-passenger bookings in one call; remove the raw book primitive).

## Iteration cand_0003 (final — 3/3)
- Strategy tried: with TWO prior rejects (cand_0001 +0.100, cand_0002 +0.117) both +Δ / zero-damage / all-tasks-unresolved, I treated this as a measurement-POWER plateau (the gate's own words both times: "the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign"). So I kept cand_0002's entire edit set verbatim and added exactly ONE new thing: a deterministic in-body payment-method-count guard on `book_reservation`. Not yet scored.
- Key process lesson (the one worth carrying): on a hill-climb:all gate with only 3 trials/task, a real but modest per-task effect never clears ~2·SE, so a mean gain of +0.1 reads as "unresolved" and gets rejected even with zero regressions. The counter-move is to maximize the SIZE of the per-TRIAL effect, and the strongest size-per-blast-radius lever is a DETERMINISTIC in-body WRITE guard that enforces a policy rule the engine does not check (so the failing trial flips every single time, not probabilistically). Rank levers by compliance-independence: deterministic code guard on the write path > unskippable return enrichment on an always-called read > new optional read tool > prose. I walked exactly down this ladder across the three iterations.
- Plateau/stall signal: two flat zero-damage rejects. The lever I switched to this round was the top rung I had not yet pulled — a second deterministic write guard (payment-count) — because the cancel-flown guard was the only true write-path guard in cand_0002 and the biggest remaining cluster (B) had none.
- What to try next (if this is also rejected with no damage): stop adding information-shaped edits — the +Δ is real and the problem is trial count, not edit quality. Either (a) ship a composite split-booking WRITE tool that removes the raw `book_reservation` primitive and emits the N one-passenger reservations itself (the last compliance-independent lever for cluster B), or (b) if the harness allows, re-measure the current candidate with more trials/task to resolve the +Δ the gate keeps seeing. Do NOT spend another iteration re-nudging prose.
